evidence.title: 御製前湖詩
evidence.excerpt_zh: 乾隆二十八年御製前湖詩　御園之前本無湖而今疏濬胡稱乎石衢之右地下濕邇年遭潦水占諸衢左亦不大高衍徃來車馬愁泥塗因卑為澤事惟半取右益左功倍俱歉嵗受僱兼代賑三冬畚鍤集衆徒役成春水有所受路東濘去誠坦途一舉三得惠不費對敭來者咸歡娛蓋聞王者無私事有事皆應史筆書此非綴景漫修剔什用播告賢與愚
evidence.summary: Explains that no lake originally lay before the gate; low ground west of the road flooded, so in a famine-relief works earth was moved east to raise the road and the hollow became a lake.

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 正大光明
evidence.excerpt_zh: 大宫門前輦道東西皆有湖是為前湖（圓明園冊）臣等謹按前湖西岸有石刻御製前湖詩
evidence.summary: The lake called 前湖 Front Lake lies east and west of the carriage road before the main gate; the compilers record a stone-cut poem on its west bank.

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 九洲清晏
evidence.excerpt_zh: 正大光明後有湖亦稱前湖湖正北為圓明園殿五楹後為奉三無私殿七楹又後為九州清宴殿七楹東為天地一家春西為樂安和又西為清暉閣閣前為露香齋左為茹古堂為松雲樓右為涵徳書屋（圓明園冊）臣等謹按九州清宴額世宗御書四十景之一也前第一層殿恭懸聖祖御書圓明園額聨曰每對青山緑水㑹心處一邱一壑總自天恩浩蕩常從霽月光風悦目時一草一木莫非帝徳高深世宗藩邸時書聨曰恤小民之依所其無逸稽古人之徳彰厥有常皇上御書第二層為奉三無私殿内恭懸皇上御書聖祖仁皇帝聖訓曰天下之治亂休咎皆係人主之一身一心政令之設必當遠慮深謀以防後悔周詳籌度計及久長不可為近名邀利之舉不可用一已偏執之見採羣言以廣益合衆志以成城始為無偏無黨之道孝者百行之原不孝之人斷不可用義者萬事之本非義之事必不可為孝以立身義以制事無是二者雖君臣父子不能保也世宗憲皇帝聖訓曰敬天法祖勤政親賢愛民擇吏除暴安良勿過寛柔勿過嚴猛同氣至親實為一體誠心友愛休戚相闗時聞正言日行正事弗為小人所誘弗為邪説所惑聖祖所貽之宗室宜親國家所用之賢良宜保自然和氣致祥綿宗社萬年之慶額曰清虚靜泰聨曰澗泉無操琴泠然善也風竹有聲畫顧而樂之寳座聨曰所無逸而居動靜適徴仁智體有常以治照臨並叶清寜皇上御書九州清宴殿後額曰蔚然深秀聨曰紅篆爐烟看氣直緑苞庭竹愛心虛與樂安和清暉閣諸額皆御書清暉閣北壁懸圓明園全圖乾隆二年命畫院郎世寜唐岱孫祐沈源張萬邦丁觀鵬恭繪御題大觀二字並題聨曰稽古重圖書義存無逸三宗訓勤民咨稼穡事著豳風七月篇
evidence.summary: North across the lake behind the audience hall: 圓明園殿 (five bays), 奉三無私殿 (seven), 九州清宴殿 (seven), with 天地一家春 to the east, 樂安和 to the west, then 清暉閣 with 露香齋, 茹古堂, 松雲樓 and 涵徳書屋. The note gives the plaques and full text of the Kangxi and Yongzheng instructions on the second hall's wall. On the north wall of 清暉閣 hung the 圓明園全圖 painted in 乾隆二年 (1737) by 郎世寜 Castiglione, 唐岱, 孫祐, 沈源, 張萬邦 and 丁觀鵬.

evidence.title: Varin: second and third throne halls
evidence.excerpt_other: On arriva, ensuite, devant un lac artificiel entouré de rochers et de montagnes rapportés, lequel était côtoyé par une route sablée ; on traversa un pont jeté sur le canal d'alimentation de ce lac, et on se retrouva dans une troisième salle du trône,
evidence.summary: A second, smaller and more elegant throne hall behind the first, then the lake and the third. Behind it salons; on the right the store of furs and robes, ahead the emperor's rooms, on the left the empress's. Varin's second hall lies before the lake, unlike Swinhoe's sequence.

evidence.title: M'Ghee: the water before the imperial apartments
evidence.excerpt_other: and on the opposite side of this miniature lake stood the imperial apartments, entered by none save members of the imperial family.
evidence.summary: From the passage turning left and to the front, a small lake with rockeries, bridged at each end, and the apartments beyond. To the right of the passage courtyards full of stores.

evidence.title: Swinhoe: from the hall to the emperor's rooms
evidence.excerpt_other: Behind the grand hall was rockery, and in rear of that again a large pond, so that a pebbled path leading over a bridge and taking a semicircular sweep of half the water, had to be traversed before you visited the next hall.
evidence.summary: About 500 yards to a smaller hall with images of Buddha in rooms each side, then another reception hall and a third, and on the left the emperor's own rooms: one moderate room with a double-seated throne, chandelier, clocks; passage to two small rooms and a spiral stair to two upper rooms with books, whose windows look down into the hall; two retiring rooms and the bedroom. The 1858 treaty lay on a table. This fits the axis 圆明园殿, 奉三无私, 九洲清晏; the ids are my reading.

evidence.title: Wolseley: from the hall to the private apartments
evidence.excerpt_other: the walk opened out upon a tolerably sized pond, on the further side of which were the private apartments of his Majesty, surrounded by the houses of his many wives, concubines, eunuchs, and servants.
evidence.summary: Walks between high planted mounds behind the hall, stone benches and rock piles, dwarf trees, rustic bridges and steps, then the pond. Wardrobes of silk and fur, jade in chests. Small armed junks on the ponds for shows watched from a tea-house (p.237).

evidence.title: Scene 3, 九洲清晏 Jiuzhou Qingyan: the emperor's apartments
evidence.excerpt_other: The island occupied by the imperial residence is the largest of all and is so covered with buildings and courtyards that there is room for only a little ornamental rock work and almost no artificial hills.
evidence.summary: On the island north of the hall across the Front Lake: 圆明园殿 on the south, a court, a seven-bay hall, a second court, then 九洲清晏 facing the Back Lake. The 1737 map by Castiglione and five Chinese artists hung in 清晖阁 in the western half. Nine islands, scenes 3 to 11, each with two to four bridges. Note 30: a pasted sheet on the Official Map shows a later rearrangement here.
